text:
Alex: Morning — quick async standup. Yesterday: rolled KV-evict tweak to canary, ran through the batcher logs, trimmed some noisy alerts. Blockers: still seeing intermittent 504s from model-proxy under sustained bursts; suspect batching backlog / connection limits. Today: follow up on autoscaler config, open CR ping for PR #432, coordinate handoff. @Maya can you peek at the canary metrics when you get a sec? :coffee:

Maya: On it. I pushed a small probe to the canary to capture 1s percentiles. Also added a prom query to surface the 504 spike: ```sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="model-proxy",status="504"}[5m])) by (instance)```

OpsBot: OpsBot: PagerDuty INC123456 created (high 504 rate on model-proxy). Assigned to Liam.

Liam: Taking INC123456. Quick log grep shows repeated `Upstream read timeout` from proxy -> model-backend. Running a quick trace now. Temp mitigation: bumped proxy keepalive and increased connection pool in staging.

Jordan: Rebased PR #432 (kv-evict backpressure fixes) and added a short integration test. @Alex can you review when free? Small change so shouldn't block hotfix.

Alex: Will review PR #432 in the next 20m. If the timeout reproduces I can grab a heapdump from the model-proxy pod. Also can you confirm if autoscaler cooldown was shortened yesterday? That might be causing oscillation.

Liam: Found a case where the batcher queue hits max_inflight then backoffs; causes bursts of requests to time out. Quick fix staged: increase `max_inflight` and add better backpressure. Applying to canary now. If that clears the 504s we promote.

Maya: Deploy plan: if 504 rate drops below 1% for 15m, promote. If it holds above 3% for 10m, rollback and mute noisy alert. I added the check in the canary dashboard.

DeployBot: DeployBot: Canary deployment started: kv-evict-1.2.3 -> cluster-us-east-1 (canary nodes: 3).

Liam: Canary shows improvement after `max_inflight` bump — 1m 504 rate down ~70%. Logs point to a small threadpool limit in model-proxy config. I'll push the threadpool bump to prod with a short rollout window.

Alex: Nice. Action items: 1) Liam — prod rollout + link runbook to INC123456 (please add commands you ran). 2) Maya — add SLO metric (error_budget_burn rate) to the midshift dashboard and create a quick alert refinement PR. 3) Jordan — follow up on PR #432 CR. 4) Me — draft short blameless note for the incident.

Jordan: Acknowledged. I'll pick up CR review after lunch. Also FYI I shortened the service restart probe to 30s in staging to speed recovery tests.

Liam: Runbook note added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/504-batcher — includes grep + curl checks and the temp `max_inflight` bump steps. Commands I ran: ```kubectl -n infra exec -it pod/model-proxy-xyz -- /bin/sh -c 'grep -i "timeout" /var/log/proxy.log' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-proxy```

Maya: I've scheduled a tiny follow-up ticket in SLO tracker for alert tuning (link: https://redwood.internal/slo/alerts/patch-847). Also pinging next oncall: @Jordan you're up after Liam for handoff at 18:00 UTC.

Jordan: Got it — will take handoff at 18:00 UTC.

Alex: Thanks everyone. If anything regresses tag #inc-504 and @here. Otherwise I'll post a short summary once PRs go green. :thumbsup:
